findings.issue: The resumability test still does not specify HOW the thread is interrupted. The text says 'interrupt (kill thread)' — but killing a live thread in Python is not straightforward and can leave SQLite in a partially-written state (mid-transaction). Round 1 flagged this; the round 2 update added 'no duplicate task_results rows, no extra LLM calls' assertions, but the interrupt mechanism remains undefined. Without a concrete mechanism, implementing agents will make different assumptions, some of which will produce flaky or non-reproducible tests.
findings.recommendation: Specify the interrupt mechanism explicitly. The safest approach for a test: after 3 of 5 students reach status=processed, programmatically set a stop flag on the ProcessingThread (e.g., thread.stop_flag.set()), let the thread exit cleanly, then restart it. Alternatively: pre-populate 3 students in SQLite as status=processed before the first run, so the thread only processes 2. Both are deterministic and do not rely on OS-level thread killing.

findings.location: Agent Verification Plan — AVP table vs. E2E=None decision

summary: Round 2 fixes all 5 critical gaps from round 1. Remaining issues: the resumability interrupt mechanism is still underspecified (critical — will cause flaky tests), test_queue_processor.py scope is still absent from the Testing Strategy (warning), the Playwright/AVP contradiction is unresolved (warning), LLM fixture files are still not enumerated (warning), the Drive download error integration test is still missing (warning), the PENDING column behavior sub-cases in test_exporter.py are still absent (warning), and the LLM batching unit test is still missing (warning). No new critical gaps were introduced by the round 2 changes.
